state:
**Goal `ext-tooling` — `nvs ext` builds, inspects, tests and pins an extension, and a bundle carries one — Stages 2 to 6 are on disk; Stage 7 is next.** M9. No floor is carried: the suites, the `.nvst` trees and `nv verify` are the safety net, and goals `ext-host`, `ext-compiler` and `ext-grants`' tests stay green as tests of the tree.

The design is ADR 0246 § 10 and the user's, and the goal file's § *Standing decisions* answers every call a session meets. No record slot: a question the record leaves is settled under AGENTS.md's priority ordering and written in `crates/nvs-cli/src/ext.rs`'s module doc.

On disk: all six `nvs ext` subcommands (`crates/nvs-cli/src/ext.rs`'s module doc, tests in `crates/nvs-cli/tests/ext_command.rs`), and `nvs build --compile` embedding each listed `.nvsx` (`crates/nvs-cli/src/bundle.rs`'s module doc). The `wasi:cli/terminal-*` imports Rust's std makes link as refusing stubs (`STUBBED` in `crates/nvs-ext/src/wasi.rs`, admitted by `Loader::imports`). `bun nv ext-templates --lang rust|c` (`tools/nv/cmd/ext-templates.ts`) writes, builds, verifies, tests and calls each template; the `ext` lane and the `ext-templates` CI job run it on three platforms (`tools/nv/test/ext-templates.test.ts`).

Checked here: the Rust leg passes end to end on Windows. Not checked: the C leg (no wasi-sdk or `wit-bindgen` on this box), and the CI job's wasi-sdk download URLs and `wit-bindgen-cli 0.62.0`, which only a CI run proves. Rust std imports nothing else outside the world (its component's import list was read by hand).
